G4483.b:
⟪λέγω⟫,
[in LXX very freq., chiefly for ⁨אמר⁩; λέγει for ⁨נְאֻם⁩, ⟦Genesis 22:16|Ge 22:16⟧, al.;]
⟪1.⟫ in Hom., ⟪to pick out⟫, ⟪gather⟫, ⟪reckon⟫, ⟪recount⟫.
⟪2.⟫ In Hdt. and Att., ⟪to say⟫, ⟪speak⟫, ⟪affirm⟫, ⟪declare⟫: absol., ⟦Acts 13:15|Ac 13:15⟧ ⟦Acts 24:10|24:10⟧; seq. orat. dir., ⟦Matthew 9:34|Mt 9:34⟧, ⟦Mark 3:11|Mk 3:11⟧, ⟦John 1:29|Jo 1:29⟧, al.; seq. ὅτι recit., ⟦Mark 3:21|Mk 3:21⟧, ⟦Luke 1:24|Lk 1:24⟧, ⟦John 6:14|Jo 6:14⟧, al.; acc. et. inf., ⟦Luke 11:18|Lk 11:18⟧, ⟦John 12:29|Jo 12:29⟧, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, ⟦Matthew 11:17|Mt 11:17⟧, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), ⟦Matthew 25:9|Mt 25:9⟧, ⟦Mark 3:33|Mk 3:33⟧, ⟦Mark 7:28|7:28⟧, ⟦Luke 24:6|Lk 24:6⟧, ⟦Luke 24:7|7⟧, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, ⟦Matthew 3:9|Mt 3:9⟧, ⟦Luke 3:8|Lk 3:8⟧, al.; of writing, ⟦2 Corinthians 8:8|II Co 8:8⟧, ⟦Philippians 4:11|Phl 4:11⟧, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, ⟦Romans 4:3|Ro 4:3⟧, ⟦James 2:23|Ja 2:23⟧, al.; c. acc. rei, ⟦Luke 8:8|Lk 8:8⟧ ⟦Luke 9:33|9:33⟧, ⟦John 5:34|Jo 5:34⟧, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369 f.), ⟦Matthew 27:11|Mt 27:11⟧, ⟦Mark 15:2|Mk 15:2⟧, ⟦Luke 23:3|Lk 23:3⟧, ⟦John 18:37|Jo 18:37⟧; c. dat. pers., seq. orat. dir., ⟦Matthew 8:20|Mt 8:20⟧, ⟦Mark 2:17|Mk 2:17⟧, al. mult.; id. seq. ὅτι, ⟦Matthew 3:9|Mt 3:9⟧, al.; c. prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., ⟦Mark 4:41|Mk 4:41⟧, ⟦John 11:56|Jo 11:56⟧, ⟦Hebrews 9:5|He 9:5⟧, al.; ⟪to mean⟫ (cl.), ⟦Mark 14:71|Mk 14:71⟧, ⟦John 6:71|Jo 6:71⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 10:29|I Co 10:29⟧, al.; ⟪to call⟫, ⟪name⟫, ⟦Mark 10:18|Mk 10:18⟧; pass., ⟦Matthew 9:9|Mt 9:9⟧, ⟦Mark 15:7|Mk 15:7⟧, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω).
SYN.: λαλέω, which refers to the utterance, as λέγω to the meaning of what is said, its correspondence with thought (Tr., Syn., Ixxvi; Thayer, s.v. λαλέω).
a: The Words of Jesus, by G. Dalman. English Edition. T. & T. Clark, 1902
Commentaries on the Gospel according to St. Mark (Third Edition, 1909) and the Apocalypse of St. John, by H. B. Swete. Macmillan, 1906
Synonyms of the N. T. , by R. C. Trench. Ninth Edition. Macmillan, 1880

G4400.b:
⟪προ-χειρίζω⟫
(< πρόχειρος, at hand), [in LXX: ⟦Exodus 4:13|Ex 4:13⟧ (⁨שׁלח⁩), ⟦Joshua 3:12|Jos 3:12⟧ (⁨לקח⁩), ⟦Daniel 3:22|Da LXX 3:22⟧, II Mac 3:7 8:9 14:12 A*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to put into the hand⟫, ⟪deliver up⟫: pass., ⟦Acts 3:20|Ac 3:20⟧.
⟪2.⟫ More freq. as depon., -ομαι, ⟪to take into one's hand⟫; hence, metaph., ⟪to propose⟫, ⟪determine⟫, ⟪choose⟫: c. inf., ⟦Acts 22:14|Ac 22:14⟧; c. acc. pers., ⟦Acts 26:16|Ac 26:16⟧.†

G4403.b: * ⟪πρύμνα⟫, -ης, ἡ, prop. fem. of adj. πρύμνος, -η, -ον, (sc. ναῦς), ⟪the hindmost part⟫ of a ship, ⟪the stern⟫: ⟦Mark 4:38|Mk 4:38⟧, ⟦Acts 27:29|Ac 27:29⟧; opp. to πρῷρα, ⟦Acts 27:41|Ac 27:41⟧.†

G4404.b:
⟪πρωί⟫ (Rec. πρωΐ), adv.
(< πρό), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨בֹּקֶר⁩, ⁨בַּבֹּקֶר⁩;] ⟪in the morning⟫, ⟪early⟫: ⟦Matthew 16:3|Mt 16:3⟧ (R, txt.) ⟦Matthew 21:18|21:18⟧, ⟦Mark 1:35|Mk 1:35⟧ ⟦Mark 11:20|11:20⟧ ⟦Mark 13:35|13:35⟧ ⟦Mark 15:1|15:1⟧ ⟦Mark 16:9|16:[9]⟧, ⟦John 18:28|Jo 18:28⟧ ⟦John 20:1|20:1⟧; λίαν π., ⟦Mark 16:2|Mk 16:2⟧; ἅμα π., ⟦Matthew 20:1|Mt 20:1⟧; ἀπὸ π. (cf. ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν, ⟦Exodus 18:13|Ex 18:13⟧), ⟦Acts 28:23|Ac 28:23⟧.†

G4407.b:
† ⟪πρωινός⟫
(Rec. -ϊνος, v. WH, App., ή, -όν (< πρωί), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨בֹּקֶר⁩;] = cl. πρώιος, ⟪at early morn⟫, ⟪early⟫: ἀστήρ, ⟦Revelation 2:28|Re 2:28⟧ ⟦Revelation 22:16|22:16⟧.†
a: The N.T. in the original Greek, by B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort. Vol. II, Introduction and Appendix. Macmillan, 1881

G4408.b: * ⟪πρῷρα⟫ (Rec. incorrectly πρώρα, v. Bl., § 3, 3; LS, s.v.), -ης (for Att. -ας, v. Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, l 2), ἡ, the forward part of a ship, ⟪the prow⟫: ⟦Acts 27:30|Ac 27:30⟧; opp. to πρύμνα, ⟦Acts 27:41|Ac 27:41⟧.†
a: A Greek-English Lexicon, by H. G. Liddell and R. Scott. Seventh Edition. Harper, 1889
Grammatik der gr. Papyri aus der Ptolemäerzeit, by E. Mayser. Leipzig, 1906

G4409.b:
⟪πρωτεύω⟫
(< πρῶτος), [in LXX: ⟦Ezra 5:11|Es 5:11⟧, II Mac 6:18 13:15*;] ⟪to be first⟫, ⟪pre-eminent⟫, ⟪have the first place⟫: ⟦Colossians 1:18|Col 1:18⟧.†

G4410.b:
*† ⟪πρωτοκαθεδρία⟫, -ας, ἡ
(< πρῶιος, καθέδρα), ⟪the chief seat⟫: ⟦Matthew 23:6|Mt 23:6⟧, ⟦Mark 12:39|Mk 12:39⟧ (v. Swete, in l.), ⟦Luke 11:43|Lk 11:43⟧ ⟦Luke 20:46|20:46⟧.†
a: Commentaries on the Gospel according to St. Mark (Third Edition, 1909) and the Apocalypse of St. John, by H. B. Swete. Macmillan, 1906

G4411.b: *† ⟪πρωτο-κλισία⟫, -ας, ἡ, ⟪the chief place⟫ at table (v. Swete, ⟦Mark 12:39|Mk 12:39⟧): ⟦Matthew 23:6|Mt 23:6⟧, ⟦Mark 12:39|Mk 12:39⟧, ⟦Luke 14:7|Lk 14:7⟧, ⟦Luke 14:8|8⟧ ⟦Luke 20:46|20:46⟧.†
a: Commentaries on the Gospel according to St. Mark (Third Edition, 1909) and the Apocalypse of St. John, by H. B. Swete. Macmillan, 1906

G4414.b:
⟪πρωτοστάτης⟫, -ου, ὁ
(< πρῶτος, ἵστημι), [in LXX: ⟦Job 15:24|Jb 15:24⟧ AB*;] prop., of soldiers, ⟪one who stands first⟫, ⟪one in the front rank⟫ (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaph., ⟪a leader⟫: ⟦Acts 24:5|Ac 24:5⟧.†

G4415.b:
† ⟪πρωτοτόκια⟫, -ων, τά
(< πρωτότοκος), [in LXX (with v.l. -εῖα, -εία): ⟦Genesis 25:31|Ge 25:31⟧ ff. ⟦Genesis 27:36|27:36⟧, ⟦Deuteronomy 21:17|De 21:17⟧, ⟦1 Chronicles 5:1|I Ch 5:1⟧ (⁨בְּכוֹרָה⁩)*;] ⟪the rights of the first-born⟫, ⟪birthright⟫ (= cl. ἡ πρεσβεία): ⟦Hebrews 12:16|He 12:16⟧.†

G4416.b:
⟪πρωτότοκος⟫, -ον
(< πρῶτος, τίκτω), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨בְּכוֹר⁩;] ⟪first-born⟫: ⟦Luke 2:7|Lk 2:7⟧; pl., ⟦Hebrews 11:28|He 11:28⟧. Metaph., of the priority of Christ (originally perh. a Messianic title, cf. ⟦Psalms 89:28|Ps 88 (89):28⟧, ⟦Hebrews 1:6|He 1:6⟧; v. ICC on ⟦Colossians 1:15|Col 1:15⟧): ⟦Hebrews 1:6|He 1:6⟧; π. πάσης κτίσεως, ⟦Colossians 1:15|Col 1:15⟧; ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, ⟦Romans 8:29|Ro 8:29⟧; π. (ἐκ) τ. νεκρῶν, ⟦Colossians 1:18|Col 1:18⟧, ⟦Revelation 1:5|Re 1:5⟧; pl., of the elect, ἐκκλησία πρωτοτόκων, ⟦Hebrews 12:23|He 12:23⟧.†

G4417.b:
⟪πταίω⟫,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨נגף⁩ ni.;]
⟪1.⟫ trans., ⟪to cause to stumble⟫ (⟦1 Samuel 4:3|I Ki 4:3⟧, cf. Deiss., BS, 681).
⟪2.⟫ Intrans., ⟪to stumble⟫. Metaph., in moral sense, ⟦Romans 11:11|Ro 11:11⟧, ⟦James 2:10|Ja 2:10⟧ ⟦James 3:2|3:2⟧, ⟦2 Peter 1:10|II Pe 1:10⟧.†
a: Bible Studies, by G. A. Deissmann. Second English Edition, including Bibelstudien and Neue Bibelstudien, tr. by A. Grieve. T. & T. Clark, 1909

G4418.b:
⟪πτέρνα⟫, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX for ⁨עָקֵב⁩;] ⟪the heel⟫: fig., ἐπαίρειν τὴν π. ἐπί, ⟦John 13:18|Jo 13:18⟧(LXX).†

G4419.b:
⟪πτερύγιον⟫, -ου, -τό
(dimin. of πτέρυξ), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨כָּנָף⁩;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪a little wing⟫.
⟪2.⟫ Anything like a wing, as ⟪a turret⟫, ⟪battlement⟫: τ. ἱεροῦ, ⟦Matthew 4:5|Mt 4:5⟧, ⟦Luke 4:9|Lk 4:9⟧.†

G4420.b:
⟪πτέρυξ⟫, -υγος, ἡ
(< πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨כָּנָף⁩;] ⟪a wing⟫: of birds, ⟦Matthew 23:37|Mt 23:37⟧, ⟦Luke 13:34|Lk 13:34⟧, ⟦Revelation 12:14|Re 12:14⟧; of creatures seen in a vision, ⟦Revelation 4:8|Re 4:8⟧ ⟦Revelation 9:9|9:9⟧.†

G4421.b:
** ⟪πτηνός⟫, -ή, -όν
(< πέτομαι), [in Aq.: ⟦Job 5:7|Jb 5:7⟧*;] ⟪winged⟫; as subst., τὰ π., ⟪birds⟫: ⟦1 Corinthians 15:39|I Co 15:39⟧.†

G4422.b:
⟪πτοέω⟫, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨חתת⁩ ni.;] ⟪to terrify⟫. Pass., ⟪to be terrified⟫: ⟦Luke 21:9|Lk 21:9⟧ ⟦Luke 24:37|24:37⟧ (WH, mg., θροηθέντες).†
a: The N.T. in the original Greek, by B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort. Vol. II, Introduction and Appendix. Macmillan, 1881

G4423.b:
⟪πτόησις⟫, -εως, ἡ
(< πτοέω), [in LXX: ⟦Proverbs 3:25|Pr 3:25⟧ (⁨פַּחַד⁩), Sir 50:4 ⁨א⁩1, I Mac 3:25 R*;] ⟪a fluttering⟫, ⟪excitement⟫, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, ⟪terror⟫: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, ⟪to be afraid with⟫ (cogn. acc.) or ⟪of any terror⟫ (v. ICC, in l.): ⟦1 Peter 3:6|I Pe 3:6⟧.†

G4424.b: ⟪Πτολεμαΐς⟫, -ΐδος, ἡ, ⟪Ptolemais⟫, a maritime city of Phœnicea: ⟦Acts 21:7|Ac 21:7⟧.†

G4426.b: * ⟪πτύρομαι⟫, depon., ⟪to be startled⟫, ⟪frightened⟫: ⟦Philippians 1:28|Phl 1:28⟧. (The active πτύρω is also found in some late writers.)†

G4428.b: * ⟪πτύσσω⟫, ⟪to fold⟫; of a scroll, ⟪to roll up⟫: βιβλίον, ⟦Luke 4:20|Lk 4:20⟧ (cf. ἀνα-πτύσσω).†

a: The New Phrynichus, by W. G. Rutherford. Macmillan, 1881

G4431.b:
⟪πτῶσις⟫, -εως, ἡ
(< πίπτω), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨נֶגֶף⁩, ⁨מַפֶּלֶת⁩, and cogn. forms;] ⟪a falling⟫, ⟪fall⟫ (Plat., Plut., al.): ⟦Matthew 7:27|Mt 7:27⟧; metaph., ⟦Luke 2:34|Lk 2:34⟧.†

G4432.b:
⟪πτωχεία⟫, -ας, ἡ
(< πτωχεύω), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨עֳנִי⁩;] ⟪beggary⟫, ⟪destitution⟫: ⟦2 Corinthians 8:2|II Co 8:2⟧, ⟦2 Corinthians 8:9|9⟧, ⟦Revelation 2:9|Re 2:9⟧.†

G4433.b:
⟪πτωχεύω⟫
(< πτωχός), [in LXX: ⟦Judges 6:6|Jg 6:6⟧, ⟦Psalms 79:8|Ps 78 (79):8⟧ (⁨דּלל⁩); ⟦Judges 14:15|Jg 14:15⟧ A, ⟦Proverbs 23:21|Pr 23:21⟧ (⁨ירשׁ⁩); ⟦Psalms 34:10|Ps 33 (34):10⟧ (⁨רוּשׁ⁩), To 4:21*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to be a beggar⟫, ⟪to beg⟫ (so chiefly in cl.).
⟪2.⟫ ⟪to be poor as a beggar⟫, ⟪to be destitute⟫, ⟪poor⟫: opp. to πλούσιος ὤν, ⟦2 Corinthians 8:9|II Co 8:9⟧.†

G4434.b:
⟪πτωχός⟫, -ή, -όν
(< πτώσσω, to crouch, cower), [in LXX for ⁨עָנִי⁩, ⁨דַּל⁩, ⁨רָשׁ⁩, etc.;] of one who crouches and cowers, hence,
⟪1.⟫ as subst., ⟪a beggar⟫: ⟦Luke 14:13|Lk 14:13⟧, ⟦Luke 14:21|21⟧ ⟦Luke 16:20|16:20⟧, ⟦Luke 16:22|22⟧.
⟪2.⟫ As adj.,
	⟪(a)⟫ prop., ⟪beggarly⟫: metaph., στοιχεῖα, ⟦Galatians 4:9|Ga 4:9⟧ (v. Lft., in l.);
	⟪(b)⟫ in broader sense (opp. to πλούσιος), ⟪poor⟫: ⟦Matthew 11:5|Mt 11:5⟧ ⟦Matthew 19:21|19:21⟧ ⟦Matthew 26:9|26:9⟧, ⟦Matthew 26:11|11⟧, ⟦Mark 10:21|Mk 10:21⟧ ⟦Mark 12:42|12:42⟧, ⟦Mark 12:43|43⟧ ⟦Mark 14:5|14:5⟧, ⟦Mark 14:7|7⟧, ⟦Luke 4:18|Lk 4:18⟧ ⟦Luke 7:22|7:22⟧ ⟦Luke 18:22|18:22⟧ ⟦Luke 19:8|19:8⟧ ⟦Luke 21:3|21:3⟧, ⟦John 12:5|Jo 12:5⟧, ⟦John 21:6|6⟧, ⟦John 12:8|8⟧ ⟦John 13:29|13:29⟧, ⟦Romans 15:26|Ro 15:26⟧, ⟦2 Corinthians 6:10|II Co 6:10⟧, ⟦Galatians 2:10|Ga 2:10⟧, ⟦James 2:2|Ja 2:2⟧, ⟦James 2:3|3⟧, ⟦James 2:6|6⟧, ⟦Revelation 13:16|Re 13:16⟧; π. τ. κόσμῳ, ⟦James 2:5|Ja 2:5⟧; metaph., ⟦Luke 6:20|Lk 6:20⟧, ⟦Revelation 3:17|Re 3:17⟧; π. τ. πνεύματι, ⟦Matthew 5:3|Mt 5:3⟧.†
SYN.: πένης, q.v.
a: Commentaries on St. Paul's Epistles to the Galatians (1892); Philippians (Third Edition, 1873); and Colossians and Philemon (1892), by J. B. Lightfoot. Macmilian. Also Apostolic Fathers, by the same. 5 vols. Macmilian, 1890

G4435.b:
⟪πυγμή⟫, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX: ⟦Exodus 21:18|Ex 21:18⟧, ⟦Isaiah 58:4|Is 58:4⟧ (⁨אֶגְרוֹף⁩)*;] ⟪the fist⟫: πυγμῇ νίψασθαι τ. χεῖρας (T, πυκνά; Vg., Goth., Copt., crebro), to wash the hands with the fist (diligently, R, txt.; up to the elbow, R, mg.; the exact meaning is doubtful; v. Swete, in l.): ⟦Mark 7:3|Mk 7:3⟧.†
a: Commentaries on the Gospel according to St. Mark (Third Edition, 1909) and the Apocalypse of St. John, by H. B. Swete. Macmillan, 1906

G4436.b:
* ⟪πύθων⟫, -ωνος, ὁ,
⟪1.⟫ in cl., ⟪Python⟫, a serpent slain by Apollo, who is hence surnamed the Pythian.
⟪2.⟫ In Plut. (ii, 414 E), a name given to ventriloquist soothsayers (ἐγγαστρίμυθοι; cf. ⟦Leviticus 19:31|Le 19:31⟧ ⟦Leviticus 20:6|20:6⟧, ⟦Leviticus 20:27|27⟧, ⟦1 Samuel 28:7|I Ki 28:7⟧), and perhaps in this sense πνεῦμα πύθωνα, ⟪a python-spirit⟫: ⟦Acts 16:16|Ac 16:16⟧.†

G4437.b:
⟪πυκιός⟫, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX: ⟦Ezekiel 31:3|Ez 31:3⟧ A (⁨חֹרֶשׁ⁩), III Mac 1:28 4:10, IV Mac 12:12*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪close⟫, ⟪compact⟫, ⟪solid⟫.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪frequent⟫: ⟦1 Timothy 5:23|I Ti 5:23⟧. Neut. pl., πυκνά, as adv., ⟪much⟫, ⟪often⟫: ⟦Mark 7:3|Mk 7:3⟧ T (v.s. πυγμή), ⟦Luke 5:33|Lk 5:33⟧. Comparat., πυκνότερον, ⟪very often⟫ or ⟪so much the oftener⟫ (v. Bl., § 44, 3n): ⟦Acts 24:26|Ac 24:26⟧.†

G4438.b:
* ⟪πυκτεύω⟫
(< πύκτης, a pugilist), ⟪to box⟫: ⟦1 Corinthians 9:26|I Co 9:26⟧.†

G4439.b:
⟪πύλη⟫, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for ⁨שַׁעַר⁩ sometimes for ⁨דֶּלֶת⁩, ⁨פֶּתַח⁩;] ⟪a gate⟫: ⟦Luke 7:12|Lk 7:12⟧, ⟦Acts 9:24|Ac 9:24⟧ ⟦Acts 12:10|12:10⟧ ⟦Acts 16:13|16:13⟧, ⟦Hebrews 13:12|He 13:12⟧; ἡ Ὡραία Π. τ. ἱεροῦ, ⟦Acts 3:10|Ac 3:10⟧. Metaph., ⟦Matthew 7:13|Mt 7:13⟧, ⟦Matthew 7:14|14⟧; πύλαι ᾅδου (Wi 16:13, III Mac 5:51, and cf. κλεῖς ᾅδου, ⟦Revelation 1:18|Re 1:18⟧): ⟦Matthew 16:18|Mt 16:18⟧.†

G4440.b:
⟪πυλών⟫, -ῶνος, ὁ
(< πύλη), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨פֶּתַח⁩, ⁨שַׁעַר⁩;]
⟪1.⟫ the ⟪porch⟫ or ⟪vestibule⟫ of a house or palace: ⟦Matthew 26:71|Mt 26:71⟧, ⟦Luke 16:20|Lk 16:20⟧, ⟦Acts 10:17|Ac 10:17⟧ ⟦Acts 12:13|12:13⟧, ⟦Acts 12:14|14⟧.
⟪2.⟫ The ⟪gate-way⟫ or ⟪gate-tower⟫ of a walled town: ⟦Acts 14:13|Ac 14:13⟧, ⟦Revelation 21:12|Re 21:12⟧, ⟦Revelation 21:13|13⟧, ⟦Revelation 21:15|15⟧, ⟦Revelation 21:21|21⟧, ⟦Revelation 21:25|25⟧ ⟦Revelation 22:14|22:14⟧.†

G4441.b:
⟪πυνθάνομαι⟫,
[in LXX for ⁨דּרשׁ⁩;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to inquire⟫: c. acc. rei, ⟦John 4:42|Jo 4:42⟧, ⟦Acts 23:20|Ac 23:20⟧; seq. quæst. indir., ⟦Matthew 2:4|Mt 2:4⟧, ⟦Luke 15:26|Lk 15:26⟧ ⟦Luke 18:36|18:36⟧, ⟦Acts 10:18|Ac 10:18⟧ ⟦Acts 21:33|21:33⟧; quæst. dir., ⟦Acts 4:7|Ac 4:7⟧ ⟦Acts 10:29|10:29⟧ ⟦Acts 23:19|23:19⟧; seq. παρά, c. gen. pers., ⟦Matthew 2:4|Mt 2:4⟧, ⟦John 4:52|Jo 4:52⟧.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪to learn⟫ by inquiry: seq. ὅτι, ⟦Acts 23:34|Ac 23:34⟧.†

⟪(b)⟫ opp. to ὄνομα (a single word), ⟪a saying, statement, word⟫ of prophecy, instruction or command (in cl., phrase): ⟦Matthew 26:75|Mt 26:75⟧, ⟦Mark 9:32|Mk 9:32⟧, ⟦Luke 1:38|Lk 1:38⟧ ⟦Luke 2:50|2:50⟧, ⟦Acts 11:16|Ac 11:16⟧, ⟦Romans 10:8|Ro 10:8⟧, ⟦Hebrews 11:3|He 11:3⟧; ῥ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), ⟦Luke 3:2|Lk 3:2⟧, ⟦Acts 11:16|Ac 11:16⟧, ⟦Ephesians 6:17|Eph 6:17⟧, ⟦Hebrews 6:5|He 6:5⟧ ⟦Hebrews 11:3|11:3⟧, ⟦1 Peter 1:25|I Pe 1:25⟧ (LXX); τὰ ῥ. τ. θεοῦ, ⟦John 3:34|Jo 3:34⟧ ⟦John 8:47|8:47⟧; ῥ. ἀργόν, ⟦Matthew 12:36|Mt 12:36⟧;ῥ. ἄρρητα, ⟦2 Corinthians 12:4|II Co 12:4⟧.

Kennedy, Sources, 124; Thackeray, Gr., 41), of that which is the subject of speech, ⟪a thing, matter⟫ (⟦Genesis 15:1|Ge 15:1⟧, ⟦Deuteronomy 17:8|De 17:8⟧, al.): ⟦Luke 1:37|Lk 1:37⟧ ⟦Luke 2:15|2:15⟧, ⟦Acts 10:37|Ac 10:37⟧; pl., ⟦Luke 1:65|Lk 1:65⟧ ⟦Luke 2:19|2:19⟧, ⟦Luke 2:51|51⟧, ⟦Acts 5:32|Ac 5:32⟧ ⟦Acts 13:42|13:42⟧

A Grammar of the O.T. in Greek I, by H. St. J. Thackeray. Cambridge, 1909

G4490.b:
*† ⟪ῥητῶς⟫ adv.
(< ῥητός, stated, specified), ⟪in stated terms, expressly⟫: ⟦1 Timothy 4:1|I Ti 4:1⟧.†

G4492.b:
⟪ῥιζόω⟫, -ῶ
(< ῥίζα), [in LXX: ⟦Isaiah 40:24|Is 40:24⟧, ⟦Jeremiah 12:2|Je 12:2⟧ (⁨שׁרשׁ⁩), Si 3:28 24:12 * ;] ⟪to cause to take root⟫. Metaph., ⟪to plant, fix firmly, establish⟫: pass. (EV, rooted), ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ⟦Ephesians 3:18|Eph 3:18 (17)⟧; ἐν Χριστῷ, ⟦Colossians 2:7|Col 2:7⟧ (cf. ἐκ ριζόω).†

G4493.b:
* ⟪ῥιπή⟫, ῆς, ἡ
(< ῥίπτω), poët. in cl., any rapid movement such as the ⟪throw or flight⟫ of a javelin, the ⟪rush⟫ of wind or flame, the ⟪flapping⟫ of wings, the ⟪twinkling⟫ of lights; ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ, the ⟪twinkling⟫ of an eye: ⟦1 Corinthians 15:52|I Co 15:52⟧ (L, mg., ῥοπή, q.v.).†

G4494.b:
⟪ῥιπίζω⟫
(< ῥιπίς, a fan) [in LXX: ⟦Daniel 2:35|Da LXX 2:35⟧ (⁨נְשָׂא⁩) * ;] primarily, ⟪to fan⟫ a fire, hence generally, ⟪to make a breeze⟫ (Plut., al.). In pass. (cf. Philo, de incer. mund., 24), ⟪to be tossed or blown by the wind⟫: of waves, ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ, ⟪blown and raised with the wind⟫ (Hort, in l.), ⟦James 1:6|Ja 1:6⟧.†
a: Commentaries on the Greek Text of the Epistle of St. James (1:1-4:7); The First Epistle of St. Peter (1:1-2:17'); and the Apocalypse of St. John (1-3), by F. J. A. Hort. Macmilian, 1898-1909

G4496.b:
⟪ῥίπτω⟫ and (⟦Acts 22:23|Ac 22:23⟧) ῥιπτέω (strengthened form; v. Veitch, s.v. ῥίπτω, fin.),
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨שׁלךְ⁩ hi. ;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to throw, cast, hurl⟫: c. acc. rei, ⟦Matthew 27:5|Mt 27:5⟧, ⟦Acts 27:19|Ac 27:19⟧, ⟦Acts 27:29|29⟧; c. acc. pers., ⟦Matthew 15:30|Mt 15:30⟧, ⟦Luke 4:35|Lk 4:35⟧; pass., ⟦Luke 17:2|Lk 17:2⟧; ptcp., ἐριμμένοι, ⟪cast down, prostrate⟫ (Polyb., al.): ⟦Matthew 9:36|Mt 9:36⟧; of garments, ⟪to throw off⟫ (for flight, Eur., Xen., al.; ὅπλα, I Mac 5:43; so EV in ⟦Acts 22:23|Ac 22:23⟧, but v. infr.).
⟪2.⟫ = ῥιπτάζω, ⟪to shake, toss, throw about⟫: τ. ἱμάτια, ⟦Acts 22:23|Ac 22:23⟧ (EGT, Page, Rackham, in l.; Field, Notes, 136; but v. supr.).†
